claim: Reproducible 50k-row / 20-column benchmark: JS gzip, ready median, scroll settle and mounted DOM cell counts for Ace Grid Core, AG Grid Community, TanStack Table+Virtual, Handsontable and React Data Grid.
quote: Ace Grid Core 1.0.15 224.5 KB 387.4 ms 28.1 ms 220 cells | AG Grid Community 35.3.1 358.7 KB 443.2 ms 29.8 ms 360 | TanStack Table + Virtual 8.21.3 78.7 KB 369.3 ms 21.7 ms 444 | Handsontable 17.1.0 380.9 KB 872.8 ms 49.8 ms 198 | React Data Grid 7.0.0-beta.57 72.3 KB 367.6 ms 21.2 ms 264

claim: The benchmark publishes fixture, adapters, package lock and raw samples so numbers can be reproduced; the README discloses the author ships Ace Grid.
quote: This repository makes the fixture, adapters, package lock, raw samples, and report public so readers can challenge or reproduce every number.

claim: Vendor benchmark (1771 Technologies, makers of LyteNyte Grid) on M4 MacBook Air / Chrome 149: 50 recorded iterations, 5% trimmed mean; 1M-row scroll LyteNyte 60 FPS, MUI 33, AG Grid 27.
quote: 50 recorded iterations in a round-robin order, with a 1-second cooldown enforced between runs

claim: Same vendor benchmark: cell-update FPS LyteNyte 51 / AG Grid 39 / MUI 22; Handsontable crashed with out-of-memory errors above ~200k rows.
quote: Handsontable's performance was measured with fewer rows because out-of-memory errors caused crashes when loading the full row counts.

claim: Competing vendor benchmark (RevoGrid) reports AG Grid at 1,297 MB and Handsontable at 1,297 MB for 100k rows, with both crashing the tab at 400k rows — contradicting AG Grid's own guidance and the LyteNyte numbers.
quote: Both AG Grid and Handsontable crashed the browser tab when attempting to handle 400,000 rows.

claim: Browsers cap the pixel height of a scroll container: 17.5M px Firefox, 33.5M px Chrome/Edge/Safari. Row virtualization is limited to 100 rows in the Community Data Grid; column virtualization is disabled when dynamic row height is on; default column overscan is 150px.
quote: Browsers set a limit on the number of pixels a scroll container can host: 17.5 million pixels on Firefox, 33.5 million pixels on Chrome, Edge, and Safari.

claim: TanStack Virtual has an open issue: lists past ~1.68M items at 20px exceed the browser max element height and the tail becomes unreachable. Headless virtualizers do not solve this for you.
quote: If the list size is long it could beat the max height value... In that way is impossible to keep scrolling until the end of the list.

claim: At 22px rows the browser element-height cap allows ~1.5M rows on Safari and ~760k on Chromium; going beyond requires replacing native scrolling with a custom scrollbar and absolute positioning.
quote: Safari: 33,554,428px / Chromium: 16,777,216px ... Elements exceeding these dimensions get truncated to the maximum value.

claim: HighTable (Hyperparam) bypasses the browser pixel cap by capping the canvas height at ~8M px and downscaling scrollbar resolution above it, plus a global-anchor/local-offset split; claims 1-pixel fidelity to ~2 trillion rows at 30px row height.
quote: set a maximum height for the canvas and downscale the scrollbar resolution above this limit

claim: AG Grid's client-side row model renders ~40 rows regardless of dataset size and the docs assert the browser runs out of memory before the grid degrades.
quote: You will not kill the grid with too much data - 100k+ rows. Rather your browser will run out of memory before the grid gets into problems.

claim: AG Grid's Server-Side Row Model moves the ceiling off the browser entirely; the reference demo serves 10M records and the limit becomes server-side.
quote: Here there are 10 million records, however the number of records is only constrained by the limits of the server-side.

claim: AG Grid batches streaming updates outside React via applyTransactionAsync with a default 50ms flush window, avoiding one render per tick.
quote: When you call applyTransactionAsync() the grid will execute the update, along with any other updates you subsequently provide using applyTransactionAsync(), after 50ms.

claim: MUI X Data Grid users report the grid degrading to unusable at ~10 row updates/second on a 400-row window, where a plain HTML table handled 100/s.
quote: With the onset of even 10 appearances per second, the application's performance significantly degrades, becoming slow and nearly unusable

claim: MUI X Data Grid's performance depends on the caller keeping every non-primitive prop referentially stable; React.memo inside the grid only helps if parent props don't change.
quote: Columns are designed to be definitions that never change once the component is mounted; otherwise, you risk losing elements like column width or order.

claim: Glide Data Grid renders cells to HTML canvas instead of DOM nodes, arguing DOM virtualization cannot survive loading/unloading hundreds of elements per frame; accessibility is acknowledged as unverified.
quote: Once you need to load/unload hundreds of DOM elements per frame nothing can save you.

claim: Glide Data Grid vendor claims: scale to millions of rows, native scrolling, hundreds of thousands of updates per second.
quote: Scale to millions of rows ... handle hundreds of thousands of updates per second

claim: The latest published release of @glideapps/glide-data-grid is 6.0.3, dated 2024-02-03 — no stable release in over two years as of July 2026.

Practitioner consensus on canvas grids: scroll performance and streaming updates are markedly better than DOM, at the cost of layout/styling primitives and re-implementing text behaviour; some argue a well-built DOM grid can match canvas.
quote: Scroll performance is much better than HTML ... Drawing on canvas is cheap compared to modifying DOM or attributes

claim: Virtualizer comparison 2026: bundle ~5KB TanStack Virtual / ~6KB react-window / ~17KB react-virtuoso; all three hold 60 FPS at 100k items; react-virtuoso auto-measures heights with ResizeObserver, react-window needs pre-measurement.
quote: All three achieve 60 FPS on modern hardware. React-window performs fastest with fixed-size lists due to mathematical position calculation.

claim: TanStack Virtual is headless: it computes indices and offsets and ships no markup, so DOM structure, measurement strategy and scroll-cap workarounds are the caller's problem.
quote: It is not a component therefore does not ship with or render any markup or styles for you.

claim: react-window was rewritten for v2 (dynamic row heights via useDynamicRowHeight, built-in auto-sizing); latest release 2.2.7 (Feb 2026), so it is no longer the abandoned fixed-height-only option.
quote: React components for efficiently rendering large lists and tabular data

claim: TanStack Table's biggest performance footgun is referential: unstable `columns`/`data` (including inline `.filter()`) cause an infinite re-render loop.
quote: Failing to give `columns` or `data` stable references can cause an infinite loop of re-renders.

claim: Aggressive memoization is not free: memoMode 'table-body' disables virtualization and most features; memoizing rows loses access to table state such as getIsSelected().
quote: If you memoize the entire table body, most features including virtualization will not work anymore, leaving you with a table that is mostly frozen after first render.

claim: Column virtualization only pays for itself at dozens of columns; below that the measurement overhead is a net loss.
quote: Virtualization only becomes necessary when you have over 50 rows or so at the same time with no pagination or dozens of columns.

claim: Handsontable's own performance guide points at pagination, fixed row/column dimensions and disabling autoRowSize/autoColumnSize — i.e. the architecture assumes a bounded working set, not a million rows.
quote: The most demanding actions are performed on load, change, and scroll events.

claim: @tanstack/react-table's latest release is 8.21.3 (Apr 2025); v9 is still not out as of July 2026.

React Compiler automatically handles memoization at build time, removing the need for manual useMemo/useCallback/React.memo — but it optimizes existing code, it cannot make a freshly-constructed array referentially stable.
quote: automatically optimizes your React application by handling memoization for you, eliminating the need for manual useMemo, useCallback, and React.memo

claim: Open MUI X issue: DataGridPro leaks ~199 MB per data refresh at 100k rows, reaching 4.7 GB after repeated refreshes; retained CellWidget instances implicate renderCell with React components.
quote: The leak appears to be internal to DataGridPro's handling of row data, particularly when using renderCell with React components.
